name: LGD-2226

lead: LGD-2226 is an oral, nonsteroidal SARM reported in 2006. Users take it hoping to add muscle and a more muscular physique with less prostate stimulation than testosterone.

It binds and activates the androgen receptor. In animals it showed anabolic effects on muscle and bone, with comparatively smaller effects on prostate weight and luteinizing hormone than testosterone. It was researched for muscle wasting and osteoporosis, not cosmetic use. No published human trial was identified.

paras: It is sold online as a research chemical in physique-focused circles, typically alongside training and diet. Reports are anecdotal.
No human safety data exist. SARMs as a class have been linked to liver enzyme elevations and hormone suppression, are banned in sport, and are unapproved by the FDA.

chain: Anabolic effect on muscle and bone
angle.text: LGD-2226 is a SARM that users take hoping to add muscle by activating the androgen receptor, with less prostate stimulation than testosterone. Animal studies showed anabolic effects on muscle and bone.

lead: LGD-2226 is an investigational, orally active, nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) of the quinolinone chemical class, reported in the medicinal chemistry literature in 2006 [1][2]. It was characterised in animal studies as an androgen receptor agonist with anabolic effects on muscle and bone and comparatively smaller effects on prostate weight and luteinizing hormone than testosterone [1][3].

It has been researched for muscle wasting and osteoporosis rather than for cosmetic purposes [1]. It is not an approved medicine, SARMs as a class are prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency, and no published human trial of LGD-2226 was identified [1][4]. Its relevance to appearance culture is limited to its use in the muscle-building (physique) segment, where SARMs are sold online as research chemicals [4][5].

paras: LGD-2226 is a potent, selective agonist of the androgen receptor. A 2007 Endocrinology paper, cited by Wikipedia, reported oral efficacy on bone, muscle and sexual function in animals with reduced impact on the prostate relative to testosterone [1]. Its chemistry is a 6-dialkylamino-4-trifluoromethylquinolin-2(1H)-one carrying two trifluoroethyl groups [1].

No studies found. The published work on LGD-2226 consists of laboratory and animal pharmacology [1], and analytical papers on how the compound or its metabolites can be detected in doping-control samples, including equine metabolism studies [3][4].

No human safety data specific to LGD-2226 were identified. Reviews of the class describe elevated liver enzymes, reduced HDL cholesterol and suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis in some trials, case reports linking recreational SARM use to liver injury, and unknown cardiovascular risk; the US FDA states that SARMs are unapproved and cannot legally be marketed as supplements or drugs. [5]

In the United States it holds investigational status only [1]. WADA has prohibited the SARM class since January 2008, and laboratory screening methods for 2-quinolinone-derived SARMs have been published [1][3]. Wikipedia notes that it was encountered as a designer drug by at least 2020 [1].
